### S0c -- PASS
*At every alpha > 1 the clump body is the body it claims to be: `phi_porosity`/`phi_union` equals the PREDICTED double count 2*(ds/d_eq)^3, and the mass Yade assembles equals the union mass.*

N: 6 production records at alpha > 1

| alpha | N cells | predicted 2(ds/d_eq)^3 | worst measured ratio | worst |ratio-pred| | worst |mass/vol - 1| |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.00 | 6 | 1.0000000000 | 1.0000000000 | 9.215e-14 | 3.331e-16 |

Bars: ratio 1e-09, mass 1e-12.

**WHAT THIS GATE CAN AND CANNOT DECIDE** (referee, 2026-09-18). It calls `shape.sub_sphere_diameter` on BOTH sides of the comparison -- the construction used it to size the members, and the prediction uses it again -- and `density_scale` is DEFINED as the reciprocal of the same quantity. So `phi_porosity/phi_union = 2*(ds/d_eq)^3` and `mass/vol_solid = 1` hold for ANY value that function returns. **This gate therefore cannot detect an error in the closed form `g(u)`**, and an earlier version of this text claimed it could. What it DOES decide is that the construction is self-consistent end to end: that Yade built members of the radius the code computed, that the clump assembly preserved them, that the density was applied, and that `utils.porosity()` is summing member volumes and nothing else -- each of which can fail independently and none of which is visible elsewhere. The closed form itself is anchored OUTSIDE this pipeline, by quadrature over the union's cross-sections, in `test_shape_campaign.py::test_clump_volume_against_independent_quadrature`, which imports none of `shape.py`'s constants and is shown able to fail on a 1 % perturbation of `g(u)`'s coefficient.

### S1 -- PASS
*The PSD does not move along the alpha axis: `cv_realised`, `d32_realised` and `d43_realised` at alpha > 1 equal those at alpha = 1 to 1e-12, at every (family, CV, seed).*

N: 9 (family, CV, seed) groups, 3 alpha-to-alpha=1 comparisons, 0 groups with no alpha = 1 rung to compare against

- worst |cv_realised(alpha) - cv_realised(1)| = **0.000e+00**
- worst |d32_realised(alpha) - d32_realised(1)| = **0.000e+00**
- worst |d43_realised(alpha) - d43_realised(1)| = **0.000e+00**

This is exact by construction -- `d_eq` is drawn from the same `psd.make_psd` at every alpha -- and is checked rather than assumed. It CAN fail: a construction that drew radii after the orientations, or one that rescaled d_eq instead of ds, would move all three.

### S5 -- NOT INFORMATIVE
*At CV = 0 every PSD family is the same delta distribution, so the CV = 0 rung is ONE cell and not three. Where two families ran it, phi is BIT-IDENTICAL; where only one did, the others alias it. The discriminating half is that at CV > 0 the families must DIFFER.*

N: 25 production records at CV = 0
N: 9 CV = 0 cells present in more than one family; 9 bit-identical; worst spread 0.000e+00
N: 0 CV > 0 cells present in more than one family; 0 DIFFER; largest family spread 0.000e+00
**The discriminating half has not been exercised** -- no CV > 0 cell is present in two families yet, so an identity at CV = 0 cannot yet be distinguished from the family flag doing nothing anywhere.
N: 0 (family, alpha, seed) phi_J values ALIASED from the family that ran the CV = 0 rung.

🔴 **THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT A SAVING, IT IS A CORRELATION.** Because the three families share their CV = 0 reference point EXACTLY, their `D = phi_J(CV_hi) - phi_J(CV 0)` are **not three independent measurements** -- they share a common subtrahend, so their errors are positively correlated and any comparison ACROSS families understates its own uncertainty if it treats them as independent. The per-family paired Delta in S3 is unaffected (it differences the same reference out on both alpha rungs); a cross-family ranking of D is not.
